Resale value of used headphones and earbuds

Popular headphones resell quickly, but generations look alike and batteries wear out. These are the details buyers check.

Updated 2026-10-12 · by FlipLens

What drives the price

  • Exact generation: models from the same line, such as Sony WH-1000XM4 and WH-1000XM5, or different AirPods generations, sell for different prices. Check the model number on the headband, case or in the settings.
  • Battery: wireless headphones and earbuds lose capacity over time; noticeably short battery life lowers the value.
  • Ear pads and tips: worn or flaking pads put buyers off, but can often be replaced.
  • Completeness: case, cable, adapter and box.
  • Authenticity: popular earbuds are often counterfeited; serial numbers and pairing behaviour help to tell.

Hygiene and earbuds

Many buyers are cautious about used in-ear products. Clean them carefully, replace silicone tips if possible and say so in the listing. A single missing earbud or a missing charging case makes a set much harder to sell.

Common mistakes

  • Confusing two generations that look almost the same.
  • Not testing noise cancelling, microphones and both sides.
  • Buying earbuds that are still linked to someone else's account.

Quick checklist

  • Model number and generation confirmed.
  • Both sides work, noise cancelling and microphone tested.
  • Battery holds a charge.
  • Case, cable and tips included.
  • Removed from the previous owner's account.

Questions

How do I tell headphone generations apart?

Read the model number printed on the headband, case or box, or in the companion app or Bluetooth settings.

Can I sell used earbuds?

Yes, but clean them, replace the tips if you can and describe their condition honestly. Complete sets with the charging case sell best.
